items.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile into East Sea

featured_image.name: Report: North Korea conducts new missile test from warship - Yahoo

items.description:
North Korea launched at least one ballistic missile eastward on Sunday, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff confirmed, in the latest in a rapid succession of weapons tests that have heightened tensions across the Korean Peninsula this year.[1][2]

The JCS said it detected the missile launch and was analyzing details of the firing, including its range and flight characteristics. The AFP, citing Yonhap, reported that the South Korean military had tracked the missile heading toward the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan.[2][3]

items.title: Trump Organization plans 70-story tower in Tbilisi, Georgia

featured_image.name: The Trump company is not banning private foreign deals, a break ...

items.description:
The Trump Organization is planning to build a roughly 70-story luxury residential tower in Tbilisi, Georgia, a project that would become the tallest building in the country's capital and mark the family business's latest international venture during Donald Trump's second term in office.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the project on Friday, with Reuters confirming that "Trump Tower Tbilisi" will be a mixed-use development branded by the Trump Organization in partnership with local developers. Details about the specific Georgian partners involved, the project's estimated cost, and its expected timeline have not yet been fully disclosed.[1][2]

items.title: U.S. prepares to board Iran-linked ships worldwide

featured_image.name: The US is ready to seize Iran-linked ships with boarding ...

items.description:
The U.S. military is preparing to board Iran-linked oil tankers and seize commercial vessels in international waters within the coming days, the Wall Street Journal reported Saturday, marking a sharp expansion of the naval pressure campaign against Tehran beyond the Middle East.[1][2][3]

The move comes as the Trump administration's Operation Economic Fury enters a new phase, extending enforcement of the naval blockade of Iranian ports — now in its sixth day — to a global maritime pursuit of vessels tied to Iran's oil trade. A temporary ceasefire between Washington and Tehran is set to expire next week.[2][3]

items.title: NATO chief Rutte calls US withdrawal speculation 'absurd'

featured_image.name: Mark Rutte takes up position as head of NATO

items.description:
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte has pushed back against growing speculation that the United States could leave the alliance, declaring in an interview published by German newspaper Welt am Sonntag that he does not foresee such a departure. "I don't see the USA leaving NATO," Rutte said, calling the speculation "absurd."[1][2]

The remarks come after weeks of heightened anxiety across European capitals following President Donald Trump's repeated threats to reconsider US membership in the nearly eight-decade-old defense bloc. Trump told Reuters in early April that he was "absolutely" considering trying to withdraw the US from NATO, criticizing allied nations for what he described as insufficient support during the war against Iran.[3][4]

items.title: Iran says no new talks until framework agreed

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Iranian official talks nuclear program with CNN

items.description:
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh on Saturday dismissed US President Donald Trump's claims about enriched uranium, declaring that Tehran will not hand over its stockpiles to the United States and that no date has been set for a new round of negotiations. Speaking to journalists on the sidelines of the Antalya Diplomatic Forum in Turkey, Khatibzadeh said the Iranians were not ready for face-to-face talks because the American negotiating position had not changed.[1][2][3]

"Until we agree on the framework, we cannot set the date," Khatibzadeh told reporters, according to Reuters. His remarks came days after Trump said on April 16 that the United States was "very close" to a deal and that Iran had "agreed to almost everything," including handing over its enriched uranium stockpile.[4][1]

items.title: Egypt, Pakistan building framework for lasting US-Iran peace

featured_image.name: Saudi, Pakistani, Egyptian FMs to join Türkiye talks at ...

items.description:
Egypt's Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty confirmed on Saturday that Egypt and Pakistan are working closely together on a framework to secure a lasting peace between the United States and Iran, as four regional powers intensify diplomacy ahead of a ceasefire deadline set to expire on April 22.[1]

Abdelatty said Egypt, Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia are coordinating on a broader regional initiative aimed at preventing further escalation and building a post-conflict security arrangement. He stressed the need to protect Gulf nations and ensure the stability of energy markets, supply chains, and food security.[1]
